title: Presumptive versus confirmatory analysis

sections.heading: The distinction
sections.body: A presumptive test indicates whether a sample is consistent with a class of substance. A confirmatory analysis, performed in an accredited laboratory using instrumental methods, is what establishes identity. The two are not interchangeable and a presumptive result does not become confirmatory by being measured more precisely.

sections.heading: What DruSight is and is not
sections.body: DruSight is a digital companion for presumptive field testing. It is not a confirmatory identification system, it is not a validated diagnostic instrument, and no accuracy, sensitivity or specificity figure is claimed for it anywhere in the application. Where such a figure would normally appear, the app displays the reason it is absent instead.

sections.heading: Why every result carries a disclaimer
sections.body: The disclaimer is not legal boilerplate. A calibrated number carries an air of authority that a subjective visual reading does not, and that authority is exactly what would make an unqualified presumptive result dangerous. The disclaimer is displayed on every result surface and cannot be dismissed.

safetyNotes: Retain the physical sample and follow your organisation's evidence-handling procedure for laboratory submission.
source: DruSight project documentation, informed by the NIST review of forensic seized-drug analysis (challenges and emerging analytical solutions).
